thm-fd-smooth-periodic-incompressible-iv:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, let $s\ge4$ be an integer, let $
u\ge0$, and let $u_0:\mathbb T^d	o\mathbb R^d$ be smooth, real, and divergence-free, where $\mathbb T^d=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ has normalized Lebesgue measure and divergence-free means $\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_j(u_0)_j=0$. For a smooth periodic $f$, set $\widehat f(k)=(2\pi)^{-d}\int_{[0,2\pi]^d}f(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,dx$, $w_k=(1+|k|^2)^{1/2}$, and $\|f\|_{H^m}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}w_k^{2m}|\widehat f(k)|^2$. Define the Leray multiplier by $P_0=I$ and $P_k=I-kk^{\mathsf T}/|k|^2$ for $k
e0$. Then there is $T>0$, depending only on $d$, $s$, and $\|u_0\|_{H^s}$ and independent of $
u$ and all higher Sobolev norms of $u_0$, and a unique smooth real field $u:[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^d	o\mathbb R^d$ satisfying
$$u(0,\cdot)=u_0,\qquad \partial_tu+P((u\cdot
abla)u)=
u\Delta u,\qquad \operatorname{div}u=0.$$
The same time $T$ works for every integer Sobolev order $m\ge s$, and $\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|u(t)\|_{H^m}<\infty$ for each such $m$. There is a unique smooth mean-zero scalar field $\pi$ for which the equivalent full equation $\partial_tu+(u\cdot
abla)u=-

u\Delta u$ holds.
def-fd-polytropic-symmetric-variables:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $\kappa>0$, $\gamma>1$, and put $a=(\gamma-1)/2$. For positive density $\rho>0$, define the polytropic pressure $p(\rho)=\kappa\rho^\gamma$, sound speed $c(\rho)=\sqrt{p'(\rho)}=\sqrt{\kappa\gamma}\,\rho^a$, and sound-speed variable $r=c/a$. The map $\rho\mapsto r$ is a smooth bijection $(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ with inverse $\rho=(ar/\sqrt{\kappa\gamma})^{1/a}$. For a velocity $u\in\mathbb R^d$, set $q=(r,u_1,\ldots,u_d)\in\mathbb R^{d+1}$. Let $e_0,e_1,\ldots,e_d$ be the standard basis of $\mathbb R^{d+1}$, with $e_0$ the scalar coordinate and $e_j$ the velocity coordinate $u_j$. Define the real matrix
$$A_j(q)=u_j I_{d+1}+ar(e_0e_j^{\mathsf T}+e_je_0^{\mathsf T}),\qquad 1\le j\le d.$$
Each $A_j(q)$ is symmetric and linear in $q$. The first-order system $q_t+\sum_{j=1}^d A_j(q)\partial_jq=0$ means the pair
$$r_t+u\cdot\nabla r+ar\,\operatorname{div}u=0,\qquad u_t+u\cdot\nabla u+ar\nabla r=0.$$
For periodic use on $Q_d=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$, take normalized measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$, Fourier coefficients $\widehat q(k)=\int q(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)$, weights $w_k=(1+|k|^2)^{1/2}$, and $\|q\|_{H^m}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}w_k^{2m}|\widehat q(k)|^2$, componentwise; real fields satisfy $\widehat q(-k)=\overline{\widehat q(k)}$. These are the periodic Fourier-space conventions used for $H^m$ in this development.
thm-fd-smooth-polytropic-euler-ivp:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $\kappa>0$, $\gamma>1$, $a=(\gamma-1)/2$, integer $s\ge4$, and smooth real periodic data $\rho_0,u_0$ on $\mathbb T^d=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$, with $\min_{x\in\mathbb T^d}\rho_0(x)>0$. Use normalized measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$, coefficients $\widehat f(k)=\int f(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)$, weights $w_k=(1+|k|^2)^{1/2}$, and componentwise norms $\|f\|_{H^m}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}w_k^{2m}|\widehat f(k)|^2$. For $\rho>0$, set $p(\rho)=\kappa\rho^\gamma$ and $r(\rho)=\sqrt{\kappa\gamma}\,\rho^a/a$. Then there is $T>0$, depending only on $d,s,\kappa,\gamma$, $\|(r(\rho_0),u_0)\|_{H^s}$, and $\min r(\rho_0)$, and a unique smooth real solution $(\rho,u)$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d$ of
$$\rho_t+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0,\qquad u_t+u\cdot\nabla u+\rho^{-1}\nabla(\kappa\rho^\gamma)=0,$$
with initial data $(\rho_0,u_0)$ and $\rho(t,x)>0$. For every integer $m\ge s$, $\sup_{0\le t\le T}(\|\rho(t)\|_{H^m}+\|u(t)\|_{H^m})<\infty$. This conditional smooth periodic theorem concerns the isentropic barotropic model with strictly positive density; it asserts no continuation through vacuum or shocks and no viscous or temperature-coupled result.
def-fd-smooth-wall-exterior-solution-dom:
## Definition

A bounded wall domain is a bounded connected open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ with $C^2$ boundary. Its classical velocity class on $[0,T]$ is $C^1([0,T];C^2(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$; a pressure in this class is continuous in time with one continuous spatial derivative. The boundary normal $n$ is the outward unit normal. A no-slip trace is $u|_{\partial\Omega}=0$, a prescribed moving-wall trace is $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$, and an impermeable trace is $u\cdot n=0$; these are distinct boundary data.

An exterior domain is $\Omega_{\mathrm{ext}}=\mathbb R^3\setminus K$, where $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ is compact with $C^2$ boundary and $\Omega_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is connected. The exterior classical velocity and pressure classes have the same local regularity up to $\partial K$ on every compact spatial subset. The domain definition alone imposes no condition at infinity. An exterior energy argument must state additional decay or weighted-space hypotheses. We call the explicit bounds $|u(t,x)|=O(|x|^{-2})$, $|\nabla u(t,x)|=O(|x|^{-3})$, and $|p(t,x)|=O(|x|^{-2})$, uniform for $t\in[0,T]$, a cutoff-decay condition; this is additional solution data, not part of the bare exterior domain, and no energy identity follows from this definition alone.
thm-fd-global-linear-acoustics:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $\rho_*>0$, $c_*>0$, and let $z_0:\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$ and $v_0:\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be smooth periodic data on the normalized torus $\mathbb T^d=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$. Use normalized measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$, coefficients $\widehat f(k)=\int f(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)$, weights $w_k=(1+|k|^2)^{1/2}$, and componentwise norms $\|f\|_{H^m}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}w_k^{2m}|\widehat f(k)|^2$. The constant-coefficient tangent system
$$z_t+\rho_*\operatorname{div}v=0,\qquad v_t+(c_*^2/\rho_*)\nabla z=0,\qquad (z,v)|_{t=0}=(z_0,v_0)$$
has a unique real $C^\infty$ solution $(z,v)$ on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb T^d$. For every integer $m\ge0$, the weighted energy $\|v(t)\|_{H^m}^2+(c_*^2/\rho_*^2)\|z(t)\|_{H^m}^2$ is constant for all $t\in\mathbb R$. This is the exact linear tangent model; it does not assert equality with a finite-amplitude nonlinear fluid evolution.
thm-fd-compatible-wall-shear-heat:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $L_1,L_2,h,
u>0$ and let $\Omega=(\mathbb R/L_1\mathbb Z)	imes(0,h)	imes(\mathbb R/L_2\mathbb Z)$ with periodic coordinates $x,z$ and no-slip walls $y=0,h$. Use product Lebesgue measure $dx\,dy\,dz$, with the quotient coordinates carrying their period-length measures. Suppose $F\in C^\infty([0,h])$ has a smooth odd $2h$-periodic extension to the real line. For $n\ge1$, define $b_n=(2/h)\int_0^hF(y)\sin(n\pi y/h)\,dy$ and
$$V(t,y)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty b_n e^{-
u(n\pi/h)^2t}\sin(n\pi y/h),\qquad t\ge0.$$
Then $u(t,x,y,z)=(V(t,y),0,0)$ is a global smooth real solution, unique among all smooth velocity solutions with the same initial data, of the incompressible periodic-channel system $u_t+u\cdot
abla u+
abla\pi=
u\Delta u$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, $u|_{y=0,h}=0$, $u(0)=(F(y),0,0)$, with mean-zero pressure $\pi=0$. The same sine series defines a smooth $2h$-periodic function of $y$ on the full real line. For every $t\ge0$, $\|u(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le e^{-
u(\pi/h)^2t}\|u(0)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$. This theorem concerns the shear solution and smooth uniqueness for the same full-flow data; it gives no global regularity theorem for perturbed three-dimensional flows.
def-fd-flat-channel-domains:
## Definition

Fix lengths $L_1,L_2>0$ and width $h>0$. Define the periodic channel
$$\Omega_{\mathrm{per}}=(\mathbb R/L_1\mathbb Z)\times(0,h)\times(\mathbb R/L_2\mathbb Z)$$
and the infinite channel
$$\Omega_{\infty}=\mathbb R\times(0,h)\times\mathbb R.$$
Both have the product Euclidean metric. On $\Omega_{\mathrm{per}}$, the first and third coordinates are periodic quotient coordinates with periods $L_1$ and $L_2$; differential operators are the ordinary coordinate operators applied to periodic lifts. On $\Omega_{\infty}$, all three coordinates are ordinary real coordinates. The closures add the two wall faces at $y=0$ and $y=h$, and no other spatial boundary is imposed. A vector field is $C^\infty$ up to these walls when it is smooth in the interior and every spatial derivative of every order extends continuously to both faces on each compact coordinate patch. Its homogeneous no-slip boundary condition is $u=0$ on the two wall faces; prescribed wall velocity $g$ means the trace condition $u=g$. The definition imposes no decay or other condition at infinity on $\Omega_{\infty}$; such conditions must be stated separately.
lem-fd-polynomial-ode-continuation:
## Statement

Let $N\ge1$, let $F:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R^N$ be a polynomial map, and let $T_*>0$. If $x\in C^1([0,T_*),\mathbb R^N)$ solves $x'(t)=F(x(t))$ and there is $R\ge0$ such that $\|x(t)\|_2\le R$ for every $0\le t<T_*$, then there are $\epsilon>0$ and a solution $\widetilde x\in C^1([0,T_*+\epsilon),\mathbb R^N)$ of the same ODE with $\widetilde x(t)=x(t)$ for $0\le t<T_*$. Thus a finite right endpoint of a bounded finite-dimensional polynomial ODE trajectory is extendible.
